articles.title: Trump’s threat to annihilate Iran to UN general assembly is stunning, even for him
articles.highlight: 但今年，他可能因公开设想消灭一个联合国会员国，而让前苏联领导人赫鲁晓夫的幽灵也黯然失色。
articles.summary: 文章说，特朗普在联合国大会的40分钟演讲中，于第11分钟宣布要对伊朗作出“重大决定”，并公开设想消灭一个联合国会员国。报道认为，这一言论可能比前苏联领导人赫鲁晓夫当年在联大的表现更令外交官不安，也显示美国与伊朗冲突的升级。值得关注的是，这涉及联合国场合下对会员国存续的公开威胁。

articles.sourceExcerpt: US president may have upstaged the ghost of Soviet leader Khrushchev by musing destruction of fellow member state Donald Trump has a habit of discomfiting delegates to the United Nations general assembly. But this year, he may have upstaged the ghost of former Soviet leader Nikita Khrushchev by openly contemplating the annihilation of a fellow UN member state. Eleven minutes into a 40-minute address, the US president announced he had “a big decision to make” over Iran, which has staged a much more determined resistance than Trump anticipated when he decided to go to war against the country in February.

articles.title: The Vampire Problem: The Paradoxical Psychology of Why It Is So Hard to Change
articles.highlight: 人生中许多重大决定，本质上是在选择去经历某些体验——因为有些事，唯有亲历才能知晓，别处无从获得。
articles.summary: 这是 The Marginalian 的一篇文章，讨论所谓「吸血鬼难题」，即改变之所以艰难的悖论式心理机制。它提出：人生中许多重大决定并非在已知选项中挑选，而是选择去获得某种只能亲历的知识。对任何要推动自己或组织改变的人来说，这一视角能解释理性权衡为何常常失灵。
articles.failureAnalysis: 关键提醒：当一段体验的价值只能通过亲历才能确认时，事前算收益的努力会失效；此时真正要判断的，是是否愿意承担这段体验本身。
articles.sourceExcerpt: "Many of [life's] big decisions involve choices to have experiences that teach us things we cannot know about from any other source but the experience itself."

zh.title: 吸血鬼难题：为何改变如此之难的心理悖论
zh.highlight: 人生中许多重大决定，本质上是在选择去经历某些体验——因为有些事，唯有亲历才能知晓，别处无从获得。
zh.summary: 这是 The Marginalian 的一篇文章，讨论所谓「吸血鬼难题」，即改变之所以艰难的悖论式心理机制。它提出：人生中许多重大决定并非在已知选项中挑选，而是选择去获得某种只能亲历的知识。对任何要推动自己或组织改变的人来说，这一视角能解释理性权衡为何常常失灵。
zh.failureAnalysis: 关键提醒：当一段体验的价值只能通过亲历才能确认时，事前算收益的努力会失效；此时真正要判断的，是是否愿意承担这段体验本身。

en.highlight: Many of life's big decisions involve choosing experiences that teach us things we cannot know about from any other source but the experience itself.
en.summary: This Marginalian piece examines the so-called 'vampire problem' — the paradoxical psychology of why change is so hard. Its core claim is that many of life's big decisions are not choices among known options, but choices to acquire knowledge available only through firsthand experience. That framing helps explain why rational cost-benefit reasoning often fails when we try to change ourselves or an organization.
en.failureAnalysis: Key takeaway: when the value of an experience can only be confirmed by living it, pre-computing the payoff breaks down; what matters is whether you are willing to bear the experience itself.
en.title: The Vampire Problem: Why Change Is So Hard

articles.title: What does it mean to have relationship ambivalence?
articles.highlight: 当一段关系同时在你心中激起强烈的正面与负面感受时，它会消耗你——以下解释其中发生了什么。
articles.summary: 这篇文章来自 Psyche，由 Francesca Righetti 撰写，讨论亲密关系中的「矛盾情绪」：对同一个人同时抱有强烈的正面与负面感受。它值得一读，因为这种状态并不罕见，却常被误读为关系有问题或自己不够坚定，理解它的机制有助于更清醒地看待自己的感受。
articles.failureAnalysis: 关键点在于：同时爱恨交织并不等于关系失败，它是一种可被辨认、可被理解的心理状态；先看清感受的来源，再做去留判断，比急着下结论更有用。

en.failureAnalysis: The key takeaway: feeling love and resentment at the same time is not itself a sign of failure, but a recognizable mental state; understanding where the feelings come from helps you judge the relationship more clearly than rushing to a verdict.

articles.title: Quoting @therealcornpop
articles.selectionReason: AI source passed freshness and evidence-chain gate: No clear evidence
articles.summary: Simon Willison 收录了 @therealcornpop 在 TikTok 上的一段评论：用 AI 代写 TikTok 和 YouTube 脚本，其实非常容易被识破。所谓 AI 腔——「不是 X 而是 Y」、三段式排比、破碎断续的短句节奏——都只是表象，真正暴露的是创作者对所谈话题没有任何观点，也没有属于自己的声音。它值得一读，因为它把「AI 味」的判断标准从措辞套路拉回到了作者本身。
articles.failureAnalysis: 想判断一段内容是否出自 AI，与其盯着用词套路，不如先问作者有没有明确立场：没有观点的内容，包装得再像样也留不下痕迹。
articles.highlight: 我能看出来你对所讲的事情没有观点：问题不在于 AI 腔，而在于你的声音里缺少那根锋利的矛。
articles.sourceExcerpt: Hey, you know it's like super obvious if you're using AI to write your scripts for TikTok and YouTube, right? [...] It's not just the general AI-isms of "it's not X, it's Y", or the rule of three, or the really weird broken staccato-like way of writing where you just say a lot of things with all these punctuation marks. and it sounds really deep, but it's not.

en.highlight: It's the lack of a definitive sort of spear of your voice — I can tell you don't have opinions about the thing you're talking about.
en.summary: Simon Willison quotes @therealcornpop on TikTok arguing that AI-written scripts for TikTok and YouTube are obvious to spot. The tell is not the familiar AI-isms — the "it's not X, it's Y" construction, the rule of three, the broken staccato rhythm — but the absence of the creator's own voice and opinions. It is worth reading because it moves the test for "AI slop" from wording patterns back to the person behind the words.
en.failureAnalysis: To judge whether text was written by AI, look for a clear stance before looking at phrasing: content with no opinions leaves no trace, however polished it sounds.
